introduction_markdown:
**General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Pure Mathematics with Statistics Paper 2 (0770/2), ADVANCED LEVEL, June 2023. Time allowed: three hours.**

Full marks may be obtained for answers to ALL questions. Mathematical formulae booklets published by the GCE Board are allowed. In calculations, you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving the answer at each stage. Calculators are allowed. Start each question on a fresh page.
incertitudes: Question 9 (ii) : le dernier rapport de la droite est imprimé « (z -.1)/-1 » (tache sur le scan) ; lu « (z - 1)/-1 », cohérent avec la droite L de la partie (i) (point (1, 2, 1), vecteur directeur (1, -1, -1)). Ce vecteur directeur est dans le noyau de M quelle que soit la lecture ; seul le point image (5, 8, 3) dépend de la constante lue au numérateur de z.
Le sujet n'imprime aucun total par question ni pour l'épreuve ; les points par partie sont recopiés tels qu'imprimés (leur somme est 103) et `points` de chaque exercice est laissé vide.
Aucun corrigé officiel n'existe : tous les corrigés sont rédigés et chaque valeur numérique a été recalculée par script (sympy).
Scan de 3 pages (page de garde + 2 pages de questions) : les questions 1 à 10 sont complètes et se suivent, aucune page ne semble manquer.

questions.enonce_markdown: Given the plane $\Pi : x - 2y - z = 4$ and the line $L : \dfrac{x - 2}{3} = \dfrac{y + 4}{1} = \dfrac{z - 1}{-1}$, find the sine of the acute angle between $\Pi$ and $L$. (3 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
A normal to $\Pi$ is $\mathbf{n} = \mathbf{i} - 2\mathbf{j} - \mathbf{k}$, and a direction vector of $L$ is $\mathbf{d} = 3\mathbf{i} + \mathbf{j} - \mathbf{k}$.

The angle $\varphi$ between a line and a plane satisfies $\sin\varphi = \dfrac{|\mathbf{n}\cdot\mathbf{d}|}{|\mathbf{n}|\,|\mathbf{d}|}$ (the line makes with the plane the complement of the angle it makes with the normal).

$$\mathbf{n}\cdot\mathbf{d} = (1)(3) + (-2)(1) + (-1)(-1) = 3 - 2 + 1 = 2,$$
$$|\mathbf{n}| = \sqrt{1 + 4 + 1} = \sqrt6, \qquad |\mathbf{d}| = \sqrt{9 + 1 + 1} = \sqrt{11}.$$
$$\boxed{\sin\varphi = \frac{2}{\sqrt{66}} = \frac{\sqrt{66}}{33} \approx 0.246}$$
(so $\varphi \approx 14.3^\circ$).

questions.enonce_markdown: Given the line $L : \dfrac{x - 2}{3} = \dfrac{y + 4}{1} = \dfrac{z - 1}{-1}$, find the vector equation of the plane which is normal to $L$ and contains the point $(2, 3, 1)$. (3 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
The plane is normal to $L$, so the direction vector of $L$ is a normal vector of the plane: $\mathbf{n} = 3\mathbf{i} + \mathbf{j} - \mathbf{k}$.

A plane with normal $\mathbf{n}$ through the point with position vector $\mathbf{a} = 2\mathbf{i} + 3\mathbf{j} + \mathbf{k}$ is $\mathbf{r}\cdot\mathbf{n} = \mathbf{a}\cdot\mathbf{n}$:
$$\mathbf{a}\cdot\mathbf{n} = 2(3) + 3(1) + 1(-1) = 8.$$
$$\boxed{\mathbf{r}\cdot(3\mathbf{i} + \mathbf{j} - \mathbf{k}) = 8}$$
The Cartesian form is $3x + y - z = 8$ (check: $6 + 3 - 1 = 8$).

An equivalent parametric vector form uses two independent vectors perpendicular to $\mathbf{n}$, for example $(1, -3, 0)$ and $(0, 1, 1)$ (both have zero dot product with $(3, 1, -1)$):
$$\mathbf{r} = (2, 3, 1) + \lambda(1, -3, 0) + \mu(0, 1, 1), \qquad \lambda, \mu \in \mathbb{R}.$$

questions.enonce_markdown:
A linear transformation of points in 3-dimensional space is defined by the matrix $\mathbf{M}$, where
$$\mathbf{M} = \begin{pmatrix} 2 & 1 & 1 \\ 3 & 2 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & 0 \end{pmatrix}.$$
Under this transformation, find the image of the points on the line
$$\frac{x - 1}{1} = \frac{y - 2}{-1} = \frac{z - 1}{-1}.$$
(3 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
Write the line parametrically: $x = 1 + t$, $y = 2 - t$, $z = 1 - t$, i.e. $\mathbf{r} = \begin{pmatrix}1\\2\\1\end{pmatrix} + t\begin{pmatrix}1\\-1\\-1\end{pmatrix}$, $t \in \mathbb{R}$.

By linearity, the image of the point with parameter $t$ is $\mathbf{M}\mathbf{r} = \mathbf{M}\begin{pmatrix}1\\2\\1\end{pmatrix} + t\,\mathbf{M}\begin{pmatrix}1\\-1\\-1\end{pmatrix}$.

$$\mathbf{M}\begin{pmatrix}1\\2\\1\end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix}2 + 2 + 1\\ 3 + 4 + 1\\ 1 + 2 + 0\end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix}5\\8\\3\end{pmatrix}, \qquad
\mathbf{M}\begin{pmatrix}1\\-1\\-1\end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix}2 - 1 - 1\\ 3 - 2 - 1\\ 1 - 1 + 0\end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix}0\\0\\0\end{pmatrix}.$$

The direction vector of the line is mapped to the zero vector, so the parameter $t$ disappears: every point of the line has the same image.
$$\boxed{\text{The whole line is mapped to the single point } (5, 8, 3).}$$
Explanation: $\det\mathbf{M} = 2(0 - 1) - 1(0 - 1) + 1(3 - 2) = -2 + 1 + 1 = 0$, so $\mathbf{M}$ is singular, and $(1, -1, -1)$ lies in its kernel, which is why a line collapses to a point.
